cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 5th District since 2005. Former sociology instructor and assistant dean at Appalachian State, nursery owner, Mayland Community College president, Watauga school board member and state senator (1994-2004). Has chaired the Education and Workforce and Rules committees.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $64,501 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 staff trip paid for by that foundation.
Missed 3 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.4%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 3, 2025-01-03 to 2025-01-03.

In April 2009, during House debate on the Matthew Shepard hate crimes bill, Foxx said Shepard was killed in a robbery, not because he was gay. She called the bill's use of his case a "hoax." She later said "hoax" was a poor choice of words and his death was a tragedy. She said she relied on two news reports.

After the Jan. 6 Capitol attack, a Capitol Police report said Foxx set off a House chamber metal detector, threw her bag under a table and went in to vote despite two officers trying to stop her. She was fined $5,000. She wrote that she disputed the facts. The House Ethics Committee dropped the fine.

endorsements.text: President Donald Trump endorsed Foxx's 2026 re-election bid, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances or actions by Foxx on data centers, statewide data-center bans, or homestead property tax relief. We also found nothing on limits for institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, or on growth and land conservation. Nothing turned up on her record on guns, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2026, and the pages we could read did not include her campaign's current stated platform. Reports differ on whether her state job was deputy secretary for management or assistant secretary of the Department of Administration.

cands.name: Chuck Hubbard

money.note: Individuals gave $858,308; PAC money $1,850; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Chuck Hubbard is a Wilkes County native and the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 5th District. He worked over forty years as a journalist at the Wilkes Journal-Patriot. He lost races for the NC House (District 94) in 2022 and U.S. House in 2024. He has never held office.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Hubbard lists endorsements from College Democrats of NC, Young Democrats of North Carolina and Equality NC. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Hubbard holding elected or appointed office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or school vouchers and charters. His campaign site backs public education and teachers, but we found nothing on school choice or a specific teacher raise. Where he was raised comes from his own description and his high school; no independent source on his upbringing was available. His exact birth date and the date he began living in Wilkesboro were not found.
